title: Biting Lip Emoji 🫦 Meaning: Flirty, Thirsty or Nervous?
description: The biting lip emoji 🫦 shows teeth biting a lower lip. It usually means attraction or flirting, often as a joke, and sometimes nerves. Here's how to read it.
summary: 🫦 depicts a mouth with the upper teeth pressing into the lower lip. It mainly signals desire or flirtation: finding someone attractive, teasing, or being suggestive. People also use it ironically to act seductive about ordinary things, and occasionally for anxiety or anticipation, which is the other reason people bite their lips.
meaning: Lip biting is body language for wanting something, and the emoji says the same thing in one character. Under a photo it means “you look incredibly good.” In a private chat it is an invitation to flirt back. It arrived in Emoji 14.0 in 2021 and was quickly adopted as one of the most direct ways to express attraction without typing a word.

A great deal of its use is tongue-in-cheek. People add 🫦 to deliberately unsexy statements for comic effect: “just reorganized my spreadsheet 🫦,” “he said he’d do the dishes 🫦.” The joke is the mismatch between the sultry mouth and a mundane topic. Stan accounts and meme pages use it in the same exaggerated way about celebrities, fictional characters and even food.

Unicode’s keywords for the emoji include “anxious,” “nervous” and “worried” alongside “flirting,” and that side does appear. Someone waiting for exam results or about to send a risky text might use 🫦 for jittery anticipation. This reading is much rarer than the flirtatious one, so it works best when the sentence makes the nerves explicit. Without that framing, most recipients will assume attraction and may respond in a way the sender did not intend.

It also became part of the face-building trend, as in 👁️🫦👁️, which turns the blank stare meme into an overdone smoulder. Whether sincere or ironic, 🫦 is heavier than 😏 or 😉. Those hint; this one states. The emoji leaves little room for plausible deniability, which is why the ironic use depends on a topic that is plainly not sexy, and why sincere use is best saved for someone who has already shown they are interested.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Between partners or people already flirting, 🫦 is a clear signal of physical attraction and can steer a conversation in a sexual direction. Friends use it with each other as a joke, hyping up a new outfit or pretending to swoon. If you are unsure which is intended, the sender’s usual humor is the best guide.

contexts.label: On TikTok and Instagram
contexts.body: It is a fixture of thirst comments under attractive creators’ videos and fan edits, and of captions on confident selfies. The ironic version is just as common: comments like “the way he parallel parked 🫦” parody thirst culture. Brands targeting younger audiences sometimes use it to make a product sound irresistible.

contexts.label: From a crush
contexts.body: This is about as unambiguous as emoji flirting gets. If someone you like sends 🫦 in response to your photo or a suggestive message, they are attracted to you and comfortable showing it. The one exception is a person who uses it as a joke with everybody, in which case it is humor first.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: It does not belong in professional communication. Even as a joke, an emoji that primarily signals sexual interest can make colleagues uncomfortable and could be taken as harassment. Save the ironic 🫦 for friends outside the work chat. If a colleague sends it to you and it is unwelcome, it is reasonable to say so.

examples.meaning: Telling someone they look very attractive in what they are wearing.
Jokingly swooning over a small considerate act.
A suggestive invitation with romantic or sexual intent.

examples.text: Just meal prepped for the whole week 🫦
examples.meaning: Ironic use, pretending a boring accomplishment is seductive.
Playfully ogling someone’s photo with an exaggerated stare.

combos.meaning: Someone or something is extremely hot.
An exaggerated seductive stare, usually played for laughs.
Checking someone out and liking what you see.
Overwhelmed by how attractive someone is.

confusedWith.difference: 👄 is a closed pair of lips with no teeth showing, used for kisses, beauty and speech. 🫦 adds the bite, which shifts the meaning firmly toward desire or tension.
😏 is a sly half-smile that implies innuendo or smugness. 🫦 skips the implication and shows physical attraction directly, so it reads as more intense.
😬 bares clenched teeth to show awkwardness or nerves. If you want to express anxiety, 😬 is clearer; 🫦 will be read as flirting by most people.

avoid: Never use it with coworkers, clients or anyone in a professional relationship.
Do not send it to someone who has not shown interest in you, because it is openly sexual.
Avoid it for real anxiety unless the context is obvious, since most readers assume the flirty meaning.
design: The emoji shows a mouth with red or pink lips, the upper teeth visible and biting down on one side of the lower lip. Vendors agree on the concept and differ in details such as lip color, how many teeth appear and which side is bitten. There is no face around it, and it has no skin tone variants.

faqs.q: What does 🫦 mean from a guy?
faqs.a: He finds you attractive or is flirting. Sent after a photo, it is a compliment on your looks; in conversation, it suggests he is thinking about you romantically or sexually. Some guys use it purely as a joke with friends, so consider how he normally texts.

faqs.q: What does 🫦 mean from a girl?
faqs.a: Usually the same: attraction, flirting or playful thirst. Girls also use it constantly with friends to hype each other up, as in “okay outfit 🫦,” which is supportive rather than romantic. Directed at you one-on-one with flirty wording, it likely signals real interest.

faqs.q: Is the biting lip emoji always sexual?
faqs.a: No, but that is its default reading. It is frequently ironic, used to make ordinary things sound seductive for humor, and it can express nervousness. Because the sexual meaning is so well known, it is safest to use it only where that interpretation would not cause problems.
The biting lip emoji was approved as part of Emoji 14.0 in 2021 and appeared on phones over the following months. It was released in the same set as the melting face 🫠 and heart hands 🫶.
